tagline: Document your GitHub projects and decisions in Notion automatically
metaTitle: GitHub Notion Integration: Release Notes and ADRs in Notion
metaDescription: Write ADRs from PR discussions and publish release notes to Notion. GAIA keeps non-engineers informed about GitHub work. See the setup steps.
intro: Documentation is the first casualty of fast-moving engineering teams. GitHub repositories accumulate context — in commit messages, PR descriptions, and issue discussions — that never makes it into the engineering wiki in Notion. GAIA bridges the gap by automatically surfacing that intelligence in the wiki.

useCases.title: ADR documentation from PR discussions
useCases.description: When significant architectural decisions are made in PR reviews, GAIA extracts the decision and creates an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) in Notion for permanent reference.

useCases.title: Release notes in Notion
useCases.description: Every release gets a page automatically populated with merged PRs, resolved issues, and contributor list, providing a permanent changelog in your knowledge base.

useCases.title: Repository README sync
useCases.description: GAIA monitors README updates and propagates changes to the corresponding project page, keeping documentation consistent between the repository and the wiki.

useCases.title: Sprint retrospective data
useCases.description: GAIA compiles repository activity data (PRs merged, issues closed, review turnaround time) into a retrospective template before each sprint review.

useCases.title: Open issue dashboard
useCases.description: GAIA maintains a live database of open GitHub issues across repositories, organized by priority and team, giving product and engineering leadership a single view.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Notion to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your GitHub organization and Notion workspace. Define which repositories to monitor and which sections to write to.
Configure which repository events generate documentation. Start with release notes and grow to include issue tracking, ADRs, and retrospective data.
Documentation stays up to date automatically as repository activity occurs, ending the cycle of stale wikis that nobody trusts.

faqs.question: Can GAIA read existing Notion pages to avoid creating duplicates?
faqs.answer: Yes. Before creating new content, GAIA checks whether a page for the same repository, release, or topic already exists and appends to it rather than duplicating.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with private GitHub repositories?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA uses your authorized credentials and can access private repositories you have access to, subject to your organization's permissions.

faqs.question: Can non-engineers use this to stay informed about repository activity?
faqs.answer: This is one of the primary use cases. Product managers and stakeholders can get project summaries in the wiki without needing repository access or understanding the code review workflow.
